name: Probability of a UK customer buying a 'VINTAGE' item vs a 'CHRISTMAS' item.

params.condition: Country == 'United Kingdom' and Description.str.contains('VINTAGE', case=False, na=False)
Country == 'United Kingdom' and Description.str.contains('CHRISTMAS', case=False, na=False)

python_code:
# Filter for UK customers only
uk_df = df[df['Country'] == 'United Kingdom'].copy()

# Identify vintage and christmas items based on Description containing keywords
uk_df['item_type'] = None
uk_df.loc[uk_df['Description'].str.contains('VINTAGE', case=False, na=False), 'item_type'] = 'VINTAGE'
uk_df.loc[uk_df['Description'].str.contains('CHRISTMAS', case=False, na=False), 'item_type'] = 'CHRISTMAS'

# Remove rows that don't match either category
filtered_df = uk_df[uk_df['item_type'].notna()].copy()

# Count unique customers who bought each type
customer_counts = filtered_df.groupby('item_type')['Customer ID'].nunique().reset_index()
customer_counts.columns = ['item_type', 'unique_customers']

# Total unique UK customers
total_uk_customers = uk_df['Customer ID'].nunique()

# Calculate probability for each item type
customer_counts['probability'] = customer_counts['unique_customers'] / total_uk_customers

# Create result as a dictionary or series
result = customer_counts.set_index('item_type')['probability']
